- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.4), model often overshoots upward; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true values in early days of 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows mean-reversion pattern (e.g., alternating +/– swings), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–3 days ahead of true trend if sentiment is trending.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model often underestimates true volatility — increase standard deviation of forecast by 10–20% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, and sentiment is negative, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid over-optimism.
- If model forecast is < 10% below recent 7-day average, and sentiment is positive, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.
